name: The defects of mantras (mantra-doṣa)
description: Forty-nine defects that make a mantra fail to protect the practitioner — cut, obstructed, powerless, turned away, deaf, blind, nailed, paralysed, burnt, frightened, asleep, drunk, fainted, robbed of potency, child, youth, old, seedless and the rest (ŚT 2.64–70).

name: The seven obstacles to aesthetic relish (rasa-vighna)
description: Lack of credibility; being caught in the particular time and place of oneself or another; being overwhelmed by one's own pleasure or pain; lack of the means of perception; lack of clarity; non-predominance of the stable emotion; and doubt (Abhinavagupta).
antidotes: the preliminaries, music and conventions of the stage

equivalents.note: in Advaita the relish of bliss is itself an obstacle to samādhi; in poetics the obstacles are what block relish

name: The impurities of speech (vāṅ-mala, apaśabda)
description: Incorrect and corrupt word-forms and faulty pronunciation, which grammar 'heals' (VP 1.14); the Asuras were defeated for mispronunciation, and a mantra wrong in tone or letter harms the sacrificer.

name: The faults of poetry (kāvya-doṣa)
description: Faults of word, sentence, meaning and rasa that diminish poetry — rasa's soul is harmed by naming a rasa directly, by impropriety and the like (SD 1.3; KP 7).

name: The twenty-five faults of singers
description: Faults that make a singer censured — biting the teeth, shouting, hissing, fear, hesitation, trembling, gaping, a crow-like voice, losing the tāla, off-pitch notes, inattention, nasality and the rest (ŚR 3.24–26); in the body, certain petals on which the jīva rests destroy success in music (ŚR 1.2.140–144).
